docs.title: Flink Tools for Agents
docs.text:
Reusable CLI tools and Bob/Claude agent skills for managing Confluent Cloud Flink projects, SQL statements, dbt confluent projects, and Kafka on Confluent Cloud.

User may interact with an existing AI harness liek Claude Code, Codex, IBM Bob, Cursor... which itself calls LLM models. The harness exposes tools that can be directly called by a human.

Those tools are in three groups: flink project management (using Confluent dbt), Confluent cloud deployment (using sql-confluent library), and Kafka/schema registry tools for development practices areound schema and tests.

This repository includes tool implementation, LLM skill definitions and how data engineers may use those with or without AI harness.

docs.title: Quick Start For Developers
docs.text:
# Install all domains
uv sync --extra all --extra dev

# Verify entry points
uv run flink-sql-deploy --help
uv run flink-sql-manifest --help
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt --help
uv run sl-dbt --help
uv run flink-sql-cleanup --help
uv run flink-sql-register --help

docs.title: Quick Start for Data Engineer
docs.text: See the Data engineer day to day practice

docs.title: Domains
docs.text:
• Flink Deploy — deploy/undeploy Flink SQL statements, snapshot & streaming queries using python confluent-sql
  • Manifest — generate deployment manifests from SQL dirs or dbt projects
  • dbt flink project management — convert Flink DML to dbt models, scaffold and manage Flink projects
  • Kafka & Schema Registry — register schemas, manage topics and Flink tables

docs.title: Using the Skills
docs.text: See Skills for Bob/Claude for instructions on installing and using the agent skills.

docs.title: dbt Migration Tools
docs.text: Tools to convert Flink SQL DML statements into dbt streaming models, scaffold shift-left dbt projects, and generate dbt YAML from SQL files or Confluent Schema Registry schemas.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: The classical use case for Confluent Cloud Flink development is to start writing Flink SQL in the Confluent Workspace, iterating incrementally, and then committing the SQL to a git repository. Adopting dbt requires developers to manually refactor that Flink SQL into dbt template syntax, update YAML files, and validate the translation — all of which is error-prone and time-consuming.

docs.title: Entry Points
docs.text: Command Description flink-sql-migrate-dbt Migrate Flink DML to dbt models sl-dbt Scaffold and manage shift-left dbt projects

docs.title: Using with Agentic harness
docs.text:
Once you have installed the skills for your harness, you can use the following prompts, in one session of your flink project repository:

using /dbt-project create a dbt project under @tmp folder. name it db-out use data as a product structure

Equivalent to the call to: 

uv run sl-dbt init ./tools/dbt/tmp/db-out --type data-product --profile cc_flink

This will create the following folders: 

db-out
├── docs
├── IaC
├── pipelines
│   ├── dbt_project.yml
│   ├── macros
│   ├── models
│   ├── seeds
│   └── tests
├── sl_dbt.yaml
└── tools

add a data analytics product named crm in this project

Same as: 

uv run sl-dbt add-data-product ./tools/dbt/tmp/db-out crm

Now the pipelines has: 

├── pipelines
│   ├── dbt_project.yml
│   ├── macros
│   ├── models
│   │   └── crm
│   │       ├── dimensions
│   │       ├── facts
│   │       └── sources

add a table to deduplicate raw customer in sources, name it: src_customers for the crm data product

Same as: 

uv run sl-dbt add-table ./tools/dbt/tmp/db-out src_customers crm --table-type source

Which adds a table in the models: 

│   ├── models
│   │   └── crm
│   │       ├── dimensions
│   │       ├── facts
│   │       ├── schema.yml
│   │       └── sources
│   │           ├── src_customers.sql
│   │           └── src_customers.yml

docs.title: Flink DML → dbt Migration
docs.text: This section is to present the commands for the classical data engineer's use cases.

docs.title: Migrate a single file
docs.text:
# Dry-run (default)
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt migrate-one-file dml.orders.sql ./my-dbt-project

# Write output files
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt migrate-one-file dml.orders.sql ./my-dbt-project --write

# With explicit materialization and ref mapping
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt migrate-one-file dml.orders.sql ./my-dbt-project \
  --materialized streaming_table \
  --ref-table raw_orders=stg_orders \
  --write

docs.title: Migrate an entire shift-left pipeline folder
docs.text:
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt migrate-sl-folder ./pipelines/facts/orders ./my-dbt-project --write --force

# Scope run to one product subtree (only tables under .../aqem/...)
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt migrate-sl-folder ./pipelines ./my-dbt-project --product aqem --write

# With an exclusion file (one folder path per line)
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt migrate-sl-folder ./pipelines ./my-dbt-project --exclude-file ./excluded_folders.txt --write

docs.title: Resume behaviour — tracking.yml
docs.text:
migrate-sl-folder writes a tracking.yml file to the dbt project root on every --write run. It records each table's DML SHA-256, migration status (done / failed / skipped), and an optional error message.

A table is skipped when it is already marked done and its DML SHA hasn't changed — so large migrations can be safely interrupted and resumed without re-processing completed tables. Pass --force to override the skip logic and re-migrate all tables regardless of status.

docs.title: Validate the migration
docs.text:
uv run flink-sql-migrate-dbt migrate-one-file dml.orders.sql ./my-dbt-project --check \
  --dbt-project-dir ./my-dbt-project \
  --dbt-target dev

docs.title: Initialize a new project
docs.text: uv run sl-dbt init ./my-project --type data-product --profile cc_flink

docs.title: Add a data product
docs.text: uv run sl-dbt add-data-product ./my-project orders_domain

docs.title: Add a table to a data product
docs.text:
uv run sl-dbt add-table ./my-project orders orders_domain --table-type fact
uv run sl-dbt add-table ./my-project raw_orders orders_domain --table-type source
uv run sl-dbt add-table ./my-project dim_customers orders_domain --table-type dimension

docs.title: From a dbt SQL model file
docs.text: uv run python -m tools.dbt.sql_to_dbt_yaml model.sql --project-root ./my-project --yaml

docs.title: From a Confluent Schema Registry topic
docs.text:
uv run python -m tools.dbt.sr_to_dbt_yaml orders_topic \
  --output sources \
  --sr-url https://psrc-xxx.region.aws.confluent.cloud

docs.title: Flink Deploy Tools
docs.text: Deploy, undeploy, and query Flink SQL statements on Confluent Cloud using a manifest-driven workflow. It can work for dbt project or simple project with a list of flink SQL ddl and dml files.

docs.title: Entry Points
docs.text: Command Description flink-sql-deploy Deploy or undeploy statement groups flink-sql-snapshot Run a bounded snapshot query flink-sql-stream Run a continuous streaming query

docs.title: Required Environment Variables
docs.text:
FLINK_API_KEY=<key>
FLINK_API_SECRET=<secret>
FLINK_REST_ENDPOINT=<endpoint>
FLINK_ENV_ID=<env-id>
FLINK_ORG_ID=<org-id>
FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID=<pool-id>
FLINK_DATABASE_NAME=<database>
CLOUD_PROVIDER=<aws|gcp|azure>
CLOUD_REGION=<region>

docs.title: Deploy a group
docs.text:
uv run flink-sql-deploy --sql-dir ./my-pipeline deploy --group sources
uv run flink-sql-deploy --sql-dir ./my-pipeline deploy --group facts

docs.title: Undeploy a group
docs.text:
uv run flink-sql-deploy --sql-dir ./my-pipeline undeploy --group facts
uv run flink-sql-deploy --sql-dir ./my-pipeline undeploy --group sources --no-drop-tables

docs.title: List groups in a manifest
docs.text: uv run flink-sql-deploy --sql-dir ./my-pipeline groups

docs.title: Snapshot query
docs.text:
uv run flink-sql-snapshot --table orders --output table --limit 20
uv run flink-sql-snapshot --sql "SELECT count(*) FROM orders" --output json

docs.title: Streaming query
docs.text:
uv run flink-sql-stream --table orders --max-rows 50
uv run flink-sql-stream --sql "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount > 100" --output csv

docs.title: Manifest Format
docs.text: See Manifest Tools for how to generate deploy_manifest.json.

docs.title: Kafka & Schema Registry Tools
docs.text: Manage Kafka topics, register schemas in Confluent Schema Registry, and clean up Flink tables on Confluent Cloud.

docs.title: Entry Points
docs.text: Command Description flink-sql-register Register, list, or delete schemas in Schema Registry flink-sql-cleanup List Kafka topics / drop Flink tables

docs.title: Required Environment Variables
docs.text:
# Schema Registry
SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL=<url>
SCHEMA_REGISTRY_API_KEY=<key>
SCHEMA_REGISTRY_API_SECRET=<secret>

# Kafka
KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS=<brokers>
KAFKA_API_KEY=<key>
KAFKA_API_SECRET=<secret>

docs.title: Register a schema
docs.text:
# Avro schema (type inferred from file extension)
flink-sql-register register ./schemas/orders.avsc

# JSON schema with explicit subject
flink-sql-register register ./schemas/orders.json --subject orders-value --type JSON

docs.title: List registered schemas
docs.text:
flink-sql-register list
flink-sql-register list --output schema-manifest.json

docs.title: Delete schemas
docs.text:
# Soft delete (from manifest)
flink-sql-register delete --manifest schema-manifest.json --dry-run
flink-sql-register delete --manifest schema-manifest.json

# Permanent delete (resolves references first)
flink-sql-register delete --manifest schema-manifest.json --permanent --resolve-references

docs.title: Debug reference errors
docs.text: flink-sql-register debug-refs orders-value

docs.title: List topics / Flink tables
docs.text:
flink-sql-cleanup list
flink-sql-cleanup list --output drop_manifest.json --include-internal

docs.title: Drop Flink tables
docs.text:
# Edit drop_manifest.json to set "drop": true for the tables you want to remove, then:
flink-sql-cleanup drop --manifest drop_manifest.json --dry-run
flink-sql-cleanup drop --manifest drop_manifest.json

docs.title: Manifest Tools
docs.text: Generate deploy_manifest.json files that describe how Flink SQL statements should be deployed in groups and in what order.

docs.title: Entry Points
docs.text: Command Description flink-sql-manifest Generate a deploy manifest from a SQL dir or dbt project

docs.title: From a Flink SQL directory
docs.text:
# Dry-run (print manifest without writing)
flink-sql-manifest --sql-dir ./my-pipeline --dry-run

# Write deploy_manifest.json
flink-sql-manifest --sql-dir ./my-pipeline

# Overwrite an existing manifest
flink-sql-manifest --sql-dir ./my-pipeline --overwrite

docs.title: From a dbt-confluent project
docs.text:
flink-sql-manifest --sql-dir ./my-dbt-project --dbt --dry-run
flink-sql-manifest --sql-dir ./my-dbt-project --dbt --overwrite

docs.title: Manifest Structure
docs.text:
{
  "user_agent": "cc-sql-tools/0.1",
  "groups": [
    {
      "name": "sources",
      "statements": [
        { "name": "ddl.orders", "file": "sql_scripts/ddl.orders.sql", "type": "ddl" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "facts",
      "statements": [
        { "name": "dml.orders_enriched", "file": "sql_scripts/dml.orders_enriched.sql", "type": "pipeline" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: SQL Classification
docs.text:
Files are classified automatically:

Prefix / Pattern Group ddl.* ddl / table definitions dml.* pipeline / streaming inserts data.* data / seed/static data scenario.* scenario / test scenarios

docs.title: Day to day activities for a Data Engineer with the AI agents
docs.text:
As introduced in the methodology chapter, the data engineers have a lot to address during the life of a data streaming processing project. This chapter maps those activities to the tools within this repository and the agent skills to potentially use within an AI harness.

This chapter is structured by use cases, and the other descriptions in this documentation may go deeper in the command references.

The acronymes used are:

Acronym/Term Definition DSP Data Streaming Project. Groups Kafka, schema registry, Flink processing and Tableflow

docs.title: Components Involved
docs.text:
A Confluent Cloud Data Streaming Processing project includes the following components:

  • Some are managed by Site Reliability Engineers using infrastructure as code.
  • Most of the streaming logic implementations is done using Flink, and other queries mechanisms

docs.title: Create a DSP Project
docs.text:
• Create a project directory: 
    mkdir $HOME/dsp-project
cd $HOME/dsp-project
git init
  • Start your harness CLI or IDE (IBM Bob). If you use an IDE, load the project in your workspace.

  • Execute a prompt in your agent harness or run a command:

    Agent prompt using /dbt-project create a dbt project under current folder. use data as a product structure Command uv run sl-dbt init $HOME/dsp-project --type data-product --profile cc_flink

docs.title: Define / update user's .dbt/profiles.yml
docs.text:
The .dbt/profiles.yml is created when running dbt init. But it is possible to reuse connection definition without running this command each time. As an example the profile.yml include the `cc_flink connection as:

cc_flink:
  outputs:
    dev:
      cloud_provider: aws
      cloud_region: us-west-2
      compute_pool_id: lfcp-1
      dbname: j9r-kafka
      environment_id: '{{ env_var(''ENVIRONMENT_ID'') }}'
      execution_mode: streaming_query
      flink_api_key: '{{ env_var(''FLINK_API_KEY'') }}'
      flink_api_secret: '{{ env_var(''FLINK_API_SECRET'') }}'
      organization_id: '{{ env_var(''ORGANIZATION_ID'') }}'
      statement_label: dbt-confluent
      statement_name_prefix: dbt-
      threads: 1
      type: confluent
  target: dev

This can be reused between project, as each dbt_project.yml references profile: 'cc_flink'

docs.title: Add data product
docs.text:
Data product will help to group Flink pipelines related to the same appplication, same analytics metrics.

  • Execute a prompt in your agent harness or run a command:

    Agent prompt add a data analytics product named crm in this project Command `uv run sl-dbt sl-dbt add-data-product .$HOME/dsp-project crm

docs.title: Add table to a data product
docs.text: Agent prompt add a table to deduplicate raw customer in sources, name it: src_customers for the crm data product Command `uv run sl-dbt sl-dbt  add-table .$HOME/dsp-project crm --table-type source

docs.title: Create raw topics
docs.text:
To prepare dbt run, the sources is referencing exising kafka topics. Sometime, for demonstration purpose, or the topic is not yet available in the kafka cluster.

Agent prompt add a raw topic named raw_customers in the project as raws Command uv run sl-dbt add-raw-topic $HOME/dsp-project raw_customers

Then deploy the raw table

Agent prompt add a raw topic named raw_customers in the project as raws Command uv run flink-sql-deploy --sql-dir $HOME/dsp-project/pipelines/raws deploy

docs.title: Create a Flink Statement
docs.text:
The steps may looks like:

  1. Create the first version of the query in Confluent Cloud Workspace. This is relevant to get access to real data and be able to discover - prepare - validate the SQL query syntax and results. In this form data engineers use SELECT ... statement. As an example we want to deduplicate some raw_customers data. 

    WITH ranked_customers AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY customer_id
            ORDER BY updated_at DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM {{ source('raws', 'raw_customers') }}
    WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    updated_at,
    first_name,
    last_name,
    email,
    created_at
FROM ranked_customers
WHERE rn = 1

  2. Save to disk and visible in IDE 

    dsp-project
├── docs
├── IaC
├── pipelines
├── tmp-flink
│   └── src_customers.yml

  3. Run the migration to dbt from this file: 

    uv run

docs.title: Using Skills with Bob / Claude
docs.text: The skills/ directory contains SKILL.md files that teach Bob/Claude agents how to invoke the CLI tools in this repository via shell commands.

docs.title: Available Skills
docs.text: Skill File Covers flink-deploy skills/flink-deploy/SKILL.md Deploy/undeploy Flink statements, snapshot/streaming queries manifest skills/manifest/SKILL.md Generate deploy_manifest.json dbt-project skills/dbt-project/SKILL.md Migrate Flink DML → dbt, scaffold dbt projects kafka skills/kafka/SKILL.md Schema Registry, table cleanup

docs.title: Installing Skills in Bob
docs.text:
Copy or symlink the skills directory into your Bob workspace:

./scripts/link-skills.sh ~/.bob/skills
# OR
./scripts/link-skills.sh ~/.claude/skills
# other harnesses compatible with skill spec
./scripts/link-skills.sh ~/.agents/skills

Reload Bob, or start claude, pi...

docs.title: How Skills Work
docs.text:
Each skill instructs Bob to invoke the tools via uv run shell commands. The skill handles:

  1. Credential setup — checking required env vars are set before invoking any tool
  2. Workflow guidance — step-by-step instructions (e.g. generate manifest → deploy)
  3. Error interpretation — common error patterns and their resolutions
  4. Dry-run first — always suggests --dry-run before write operations

docs.title: Trigger Phrases
docs.text:
Each skill activates on specific phrases. Examples:

Phrase Skill triggered "deploy my Flink SQL" flink-deploy "generate a deploy manifest" manifest "migrate my DML to dbt" dbt-project "scaffold a dbt project" dbt-project "register my Avro schema" kafka "clean up Flink tables" kafka
